- Sanjay Gandhi pressured the Central Bank of India over loans to Maruti. 

- B. Janardhana Poojary, MoS Finance under Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi — pressured bank employees to issue loans in the 1980s.

All due process has been followed in the IDBI Bank strategic restructuring, and we have already clarified this yesterday.

2. Open the borders and legalize everyone living in America illegally to cement a permanent majority.

3. Increase the size of the Supreme Court to gain an immediate majority. 

This would result in America becoming a permanent one-party state and the end of democracy in any meaningful sense of the word.

All that is needed to ensure this doesn’t happen is 51 Republican senators in 2029. That is why you should vote for Republican senators this election. Other reasons are irrelevant compared to this one.

items.tx:
🚨🚨🚨 Americans, you carry a historic responsibility. 🚨🚨🚨

Not only toward yourselves. Toward the entire world.

Let me explain why.

I'm French. I run an AI company. I live between Paris and San Francisco, so I see both sides of the Atlantic. And I can see what's coming.

We are living through the most consequential civilizational shift in human history. AI is not another tech cycle. Within ten years it will rewrite how we work, how we learn, how we create wealth, and how we decide what is true.

AI can become the greatest instrument of freedom ever built, or the most perfect instrument of control. Same technology. The only difference is who writes the rules.

That is the choice in front of you.

On one side, the world the globalists have been dreaming of for decades. A managed society run by unelected institutions, from Brussels to Davos. Experts deciding what you may say, what you may buy, what counts as true. And now, with AI, the tools to enforce it at scale.

On the other side, a new world, far fairer. Built on reality instead of narratives. Where you can build, speak and trade without asking permission. Where we finally stop building entire systems on lies everyone can see.

If the Democrats take back power, there's a strong chance the first world wins.

How can I be so sure? Because I live in the trailer.

In Europe, the machinery is already built.

The Digital Services Act lets Brussels fine a platform up to 6% of its global revenue for failing to manage "systemic risks" as vague as "negative effects on civic discourse." The first fine ever issued under it went to X. €120 million.

The digital euro: in July, the European Parliament voted 416 to 169 to move it forward. It is now being finalized in closed-door negotiations, with a deal targeted before the end of the year and a launch aimed at 2029. A central bank currency where your financial privacy depends on rules politicians can rewrite later.

Speech under supervision. Money under supervision. Now add an AI that can read everything, everywhere, in real time.

You think it stays in Europe? The DSA already applies to your platforms. And your protection against a digital dollar today? An executive order the next president can erase with one signature, and a ban that passed the House and is still stuck in the Senate.

The Senate. Again.

You have something we don't have in Europe. A man who cannot be bought, because there is nothing left that anyone could offer him. Elon Musk.

Love him or hate him, you know he's authentic. He bought Twitter and gave you your voice back. He has been smeared, boycotted and targeted by every institution that used to own the narrative, and he never bent. He never made a deal with the devil.

When a man like that tells you everything comes down to 51 senators, you listen.

Read his post again. Two new states: four new senators. A bigger Supreme Court: a new majority overnight. Mass legalization: a new electorate. Change the rules of the game once, and you never have to win it again.

That is not a policy agenda. That is an exit from democracy. And once the door is locked from the inside, the European machine crosses the Atlantic. The speech police. The supervised money. The managed truth. All of it running on AI.

Europe was the trailer. Don't let America become the movie.

The entire West is watching you. If America falls, there is nowhere left to go. You are the last country on Earth where an ordinary citizen can still say no, and make it count.

On November 3rd, vote like the free world depends on it.

This time, it does.

October 29, 1618. Walter Raleigh asked to inspect the axe before they used it on him, ran his thumb along the edge, and said it was sharp medicine that would cure all his diseases.

Then the executioner hesitated, and Raleigh told him to strike.

He was being killed for a fifteen year old treason conviction that everyone knew was rigged, revived to satisfy the Spanish ambassador over something Raleigh's son had done in South America.

Raleigh's career under Elizabeth I was the Elizabethan age in one man. He put down a Catholic rising in Munster, became Captain of the Queen's Guard in 1587, and worked as a privateer, which is the polite term for a pirate with a royal licence.

In 1591 he secretly married Bess Throckmorton, one of Elizabeth's ladies in waiting, which the Queen regarded as a personal betrayal, and both of them went to the Tower for a month.

He bought his way back with the capture of the Madre de Deus in 1592, a Portuguese carrack whose cargo was worth a staggering amount, and in 1595 he was commissioned to go and find El Dorado.

He went to Guiana, found no golden city, and wrote a book about it that was more persuasive than the evidence warranted. That book is why he kept believing in it for the next twenty years.

Then Elizabeth died, and James I came south from Scotland with one overriding foreign policy goal, which was peace with Spain.

Raleigh was the most famous Spain-hating privateer in England. He was the opposite of everything the new reign wanted.

In 1603 he was accused of involvement in a plot to put Arbella Stuart on the throne. The trial was a disgrace even by the standards of the time. The main evidence was a confession from Lord Cobham, who retracted it and then re-made it, and Raleigh was denied the right to have Cobham brought into court to face him. The prosecutor Edward Coke abused him from the bench.

Raleigh defended himself so well that the trial started turning public opinion in his favour, which is a rare thing for a man already convicted in everyone's mind.

He was condemned, then reprieved at the last moment, and spent the next thirteen years in the Tower.

And that is where he did the work he should be remembered for. He had rooms, his wife and son with him at times, a garden and a laboratory, and he wrote The History of the World, an enormous unfinished book that got as far as 130 BC and was a bestseller for a century. It was one of Oliver Cromwell's recommended books for his son.

He also kept telling anybody who would listen that there was a gold mine in Guiana.

In 1617, James was broke. So he let Raleigh out to go and find it, with one absolute condition. Do not fight the Spanish.

The expedition was a catastrophe. Disease wrecked the crews. Raleigh fell ill and stayed in Trinidad while his son Walter led the party up the Orinoco.

They attacked the Spanish settlement of San Thomé. Walter Raleigh the younger was killed in it, along with Spanish settlers.

So Raleigh came home with no gold, no son, and a war crime against a country his king was trying to befriend.

The Spanish ambassador, the Count of Gondomar, who had enormous influence at James's court, demanded his death.

And here is the mechanism, which is the bit that makes it so cold. James did not need a new trial. Raleigh was still a condemned man under the 1603 sentence, which had only ever been suspended. All James had to do was let the original sentence take effect.

He was executed for a treason he almost certainly did not commit, in order to punish him for something he had not personally done.

items.tx:
He wrote "You're My Best Friend" for her the year they married. She raised six children while he toured the world with Queen. Fifty years later — they're still in the same house in Putney. Veronica Tetzlaff is the most private person in rock history.

On March 26th, 1971 — John Deacon walked into a college disco in London.

He had joined Queen just two months earlier. Across the room was a young woman named Veronica Tetzlaff — born in Sheffield, of Polish ancestry, studying at the Maria Assumpta Teacher Training College.

They met. They started dating.

Veronica was pursuing a teacher training course in Kensington. After a few years of dating — they married on January 18th, 1975. Veronica was already pregnant at the time of the wedding.

Queen was rising. World tours were starting. Bohemian Rhapsody was coming.

A friend who knew Veronica well said — "She didn't wear any makeup and wore fairly plain clothes. She is a lovely person, completely unpretentious. I've got the impression down the years that their children are the most important things to her."

Together they had six children — Robert in 1975, Michael in 1978, Laura in 1979, Joshua in 1983, Luke in 1992, and Cameron in 1993.

While John played bass on some of the greatest records in history — Veronica raised their family quietly. No interviews. No premieres. No fame.

She chose to live a quiet life away from public attention to raise their children — a distinction she has maintained for over fifty years.

Today — John and Veronica still live together in Putney, South West London.

John wrote "You're My Best Friend" for her in 1975 — the same year they married.

Fifty years later — the song still plays on radio stations worldwide.

And the woman it was written for has never once spoken about it publicly.

Some love stories don't need an audience.

#johndeacon #queen

qt.t:
🚨 Oleshky. Russian Propaganda and a Scenario We Have Already Seen in Donbas in 2014.

First of all, I want to draw attention to the fact that what we are seeing is not simply footage of a so-called humanitarian operation, but material produced by the Russian state news agency TASS.

In my assessment, it bears the characteristics of a propaganda product that could serve several purposes simultaneously.

The first is the domestic mobilization of Russian society.

We witnessed similar information warfare mechanisms in Donbas in 2014: the rhetoric of “liberation,” the demonization of Ukraine, accusations against the West and NATO, and the portrayal of Russia as a protector of the population.

Such narratives can sustain public support for aggression and create justifications for continuing the war.

The second is the creation of material that could be used to justify Russia’s actions in the future.

If evidence of the forced displacement of Ukrainian civilians emerges later, this footage could be used to promote the narrative that people were supposedly evacuated voluntarily and rescued.

This is precisely the risk we warned about even before the operation began.

TASS photographs date

items.tx:
🚨 OLESHKY: A HUMANITARIAN MISSION OR A LARGE-SCALE RUSSIAN INFORMATION OPERATION

What is happening around Oleshky increasingly reminds me of the information warfare mechanisms Russia used in Donbas in 2014.

And I want to draw attention not only to the humanitarian operation mediated by Melania Trump, but also to who is covering it, what narratives are being spread, and who benefits from them.

Russian state media are showing buses, ambulances, humanitarian supplies, Russian soldiers, and supposedly “rescued” civilians.

At the same time, reports are emerging in which the Ukrainian Armed Forces are accused of shelling residential buildings, laying mines, and obstructing evacuations.

A very clear narrative is being constructed:

Russia is the savior. Ukraine is the aggressor. The Russian army is the protector of civilians.

We saw something similar in 2014, when the Kremlin used the rhetoric of the “liberation of Donbas” to justify its intervention and build domestic support within Russia.

Today, these narratives could also be used to maintain public support for the war, justify Russian aggression, and encourage further military mobilization.

And now comes the most interesting part: foreign journalists.

The Russian side reports that dozens of media representatives are present, including American and other foreign journalists.

Among those whose statements are being broadcast by the Russian military television channel Zvezda is an American journalist, Rick Sanchez.

But Rick Sanchez is a presenter on RT, the Russian state-funded propaganda outlet.

His program, Sanchez Effect, is broadcast by RT itself.

Therefore, presenting Sanchez merely as an independent American journalist while concealing his professional ties to Russian state media is misleading the audience.

Having American citizenship does not make a journalist independent of the editorial policies of the media organization they work for.

And when such a journalist appears on a Russian military television channel, repeats accusations against Ukraine, and portrays Russia as a country supposedly open to peace, a legitimate question arises:

Is this independent documentation of a humanitarian operation, or the promotion of a Russian state narrative?

I am also deeply concerned about the imbalance in media coverage.

We see numerous Russian reports about humanitarian supplies, buses, and statements from Russian officials.

But where are the equally accessible, independently documented testimonies of the residents of Oleshky themselves?

Where is the full Ukrainian perspective, including accounts of life under occupation and documentation of possible violations of international humanitarian law?

Where are the guarantees that civilians can speak freely without Russian soldiers present, choose their evacuation destination voluntarily, and remain protected from forced displacement?

I am not claiming that every person appearing in these reports is lying. And humanitarian assistance must be provided to people regardless of who delivers it.

But a humanitarian mission must not become an information warfare instrument for the very state that occupies this territory.

Especially when its media coverage uses mechanisms familiar from 2014: demonizing Ukraine, portraying Russia as a savior, and using foreign voices to lend international legitimacy to that portrayal.

Melania Trump and everyone involved in this humanitarian mission must understand the risk of its outcomes being exploited by Russian propaganda.

We must examine not only how many buses arrived in Oleshky, but also where people are being taken, who controls their movements, whether independent monitoring exists, and what happens after the television cameras stop filming.

Because for Ukraine, this is not merely a question of information warfare.

It is a question of the lives, freedom, and fundamental rights of our citizens.

Humanitarian aid must save lives. It must not legitimize Russian occupation.

#Oleshky

items.tx:
Minos analyzed media coverage of the humanitarian crisis in occupied Oleshky: 2,395 publications from 1,435 sources across 46 countries between August 25 and October 6, 2026.

The monitoring showed that the first wave of attention emerged on social media — a week before major media outlets picked up the story. Private individuals accounted for 72% of the publications.

At the same time, the focus of coverage shifted: the share of publications about drone deliveries of food increased from 6% to 28%.

Russian media and pro-war Telegram channels published 162 items promoting the narrative that Ukraine was responsible for the crisis. Minos also identified unofficial pages using the names CNN News and Al Jazeera English that published identical texts almost simultaneously.

This type of monitoring helps reveal where an information wave begins, how its content changes, and who is trying to influence public perception of events.

Minos applies this approach to analyzing the information landscape surrounding companies and institutions.

Read the full analysis: https://minoscore.com/blog/oleshky-in-world-media-2026
